adhyaya.definition: Thematic division of teaching, often with a specific yoga or philosophical focus.

shloka.definition: Metrical unit of Sanskrit poetry, carrying rhythm, structure, and tradition.

parva.definition: Major division used primarily in the Mahabharata.

sarga.definition: Chapter-level division in Kavya and Ramayana.

skandha.definition: Major division used in Puranas, especially Srimad Bhagavatam.

mantra.definition: A sacred utterance, revealed sound, or prayer.

sutra.definition: A concise, compressed rule or thread of knowledge.

pada.definition: A quarter section of an Adhyaya in technical sciences.

adhikarana.definition: A complete logical argument unit (Vishaya, Samshaya, Purvapaksha, Siddhanta).

anuvada.definition: Direct rendering of the text into another language.

bhashya.definition: The most authoritative, word-by-word unpacking of a root text.

tika.definition: Commentary on a Bhashya, clarifying its depth.

vyakhyana.definition: Extended flowing elaboration making the text accessible.

tatparya.definition: The inner essence and practical application of the text.

bhavartha.definition: Interpretive extraction of the spiritual sentiment.

anvaya.definition: Grammatical reordering of Sanskrit words into prose order.
